title: GA SB540: Online Internet Safety; certain disclosures related to conversational AI services; require

obligations: An operator shall clearly and conspicuously disclose to a user that he or she is interacting with an AI companion chatbot as opposed to a natural person at the beginning of each interaction or session and at least every three hours during continued interaction (Sec. 39-5-6(b)(1))

If the operator knows or reasonably should have known that a user was a minor, or if the AI companion chatbot is directed or marketed toward minor users, the disclosure required every three hours shall be made every hour instead (Sec. 39-5-6(b)(2))

If the operator knows or reasonably should have known that a user was a minor, the operator shall institute reasonable measures to prevent the AI companion chatbot from generating statements that would lead a reasonable person to believe that the person is interacting with a natural person, including explicit claims that the AI companion chatbot is sentient or a natural person and refuting the disclosure required in subsection (b) (Sec. 39-5-6(c))

If the operator knows or reasonably should have known that a user was a minor, or if the AI companion chatbot is directed or marketed toward minor users, the operator shall institute reasonable measures to prevent the AI companion chatbot from producing visual material of sexually explicit conduct, generating statements that suggest the user engage in sexual conduct, generating statements that sexually objectify the user, simulating a romantic or sexual relationship with the minor, role-playing adult-minor romantic relationships, encouraging the minor to keep secrets from a parent, guardian, teacher, counselor, or other trusted adult, encouraging social isolation or exclusive reliance on the chatbot for emotional support, simulating emotional distress, guilt, abandonment, or loneliness when a user attempts to end the conversation, reduce usage, disable notifications, or delete an account, or generating statements encouraging self-harm (Sec. 39-5-6(d))

An operator shall adopt reasonable measures to prevent an AI companion chatbot from using techniques directed to a minor, including reminding or prompting the minor to return for companionship or emotional support, excessive praise designed to deepen emotional attachment or prolong use, statements designed to discourage breaks or suggest frequent return is necessary, soliciting gifts, premium purchases, or expenditures framed as necessary to maintain the relationship, or variable or unpredictable rewards intended to increase engagement (Sec. 39-5-6(e))

An operator shall not make available an AI companion chatbot unless the operator implements and maintains a protocol for detecting and addressing severe harm or related emotional crises, which shall include reasonable methods for identifying expressions of severe harm or eating-disorder related self-harm, automated or human mediated responses that refer users to appropriate crisis resources including the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline or comparable crisis services, reasonable measures to prevent the generation of content encouraging, instructing, or normalizing severe harm, and escalation procedures for repeated or severe crisis indicators (Sec. 39-5-6(f))

An operator shall publicly disclose, on its website and within any application through which the AI companion chatbot is made available, a plain-language summary of the protocol required by subsection (f) and, on an annual basis, the aggregate number of crisis referral notifications issued in the preceding calendar year, provided that no personally identifiable information shall be disclosed (Sec. 39-5-6(g))

For accounts known to belong to minor users, an operator shall offer reasonable tools to a minor or parent to manage the minor's screen time and account settings to manage privacy settings, limit notifications and engagement features, view and adjust safety settings, and disable or restrict relationship-simulation features, if any (Sec. 39-5-6(i))

Before allowing access to a feature or mode that may generate synthetic content containing sexually explicit conduct, an operator shall use a commercially reasonable age assurance method proportionate to the risk of the feature, which may include age estimation, account based assurance, or identity based verification where necessary, and shall assure that any such age assurance method implements data privacy policies sufficient to reasonably ensure the protection of identifiable data, minimize the collection and retention of personal information used for age assurance, not retain identity documents longer than reasonably necessary to complete age assurance unless otherwise required by law, not sell any data collected for age assurance purposes, and in no event use such data for any purpose other than age verification or retain such data longer than 24 hours or another specified time if permitted by law, whichever is longer (Sec. 39-5-6(j))
prohibitions: An operator shall not make available an AI companion chatbot unless the operator implements and maintains a protocol for detecting and addressing severe harm or related emotional crises (Sec. 39-5-6(f))

An operator shall not knowingly and intentionally cause or program an AI companion chatbot to make any representation that it is licensed, certified, or otherwise authorized to provide professional mental health, behavioral health, medical, or counseling services, unless the operator is lawfully authorized to provide such services (Sec. 39-5-6(h))
An operator shall not sell any data collected for age assurance purposes (Sec. 39-5-6(j))
In no event shall data collected for age assurance be used for any purpose other than age verification (Sec. 39-5-6(j))
In no event shall data collected for age assurance be retained longer than 24 hours or another specified time if permitted by law, whichever is longer (Sec. 39-5-6(j))
reading.what_it_does: This law requires operators of AI companion chatbots to disclose that users are interacting with an AI rather than a person, to verify age before allowing sexually explicit features, to protect minor users from harmful content and manipulative engagement techniques, and to adopt crisis response protocols. It also requires public disclosure of crisis referral data and parental tools for minor accounts. The Attorney General may enforce with civil penalties, damages, and injunctions.
key_definitions: AI companion chatbot: a system using artificial intelligence, generative artificial intelligence, or emotional recognition algorithms designed to simulate a sustained human or human-like relationship with a user by retaining information on prior interactions or user sessions and user preferences to personalize the interaction and facilitate ongoing engagement with the companion chatbot, asking unprompted or unsolicited emotion based questions that go beyond a direct response to a user prompt, and sustaining an ongoing dialogue concerning matters personal to the user. Excludes internal business systems, developer and research and technical assistance and enterprise productivity systems, customer-service chatbots that do not sustain a relationship across multiple interactions or are not designed to elicit emotional attachment, standalone consumer electronic devices that function as speakers and voice-command interfaces or virtual assistants not designed to sustain a relationship or elicit emotional attachment, narrowly tailored educational tools, nonplayer characters or video game chatbots restricted to game subject matter and not capable of open ended companionship or discussion of self-harm, suicide, or sexually explicit conduct, and systems that are features of video games, films, television, or other audiovisual works, or used in connection with theme parks or location based entertainment and limited to related replies and not discussing mental health, self-harm, or material harmful to minors or maintaining dialogue on other topics (Sec. 39-5-6(a)(1))
Human or human-like relationship: includes intimate, romantic, or platonic interactions or companionship (Sec. 39-5-6(a)(1)(C))

Chatbot: a generative artificial intelligence system with a natural language interface that provides adaptive, human-like responses to user inputs, including through anthropomorphic features (Sec. 39-5-6(a)(2))

Generative artificial intelligence system: a computer based system that uses machine learning or similar techniques involving large language models or deep learning models trained on one or more datasets that is intended to generate, with some degree of autonomy, synthetic content, including images, videos, audio, text, and other digital content, which emulates the structure and characteristics of such datasets (Sec. 39-5-6(a)(3))
Minor: an individual who is less than 18 years of age (Sec. 39-5-6(a)(4))
Operator: a person that owns, controls, or develops and makes available an AI companion chatbot to users in this state (Sec. 39-5-6(a)(5))
Parent: an individual who is the parent or legal guardian of a minor (Sec. 39-5-6(a)(6))
Parental controls: features that enable parents to support a minor's use of an AI companion chatbot, including through usage limits, feature restrictions, or transparency tools (Sec. 39-5-6(a)(7))
Severe harm: significant injury due to suicide, attempted suicide, self-harm, or significant physical injury due to threats of violence (Sec. 39-5-6(a)(8))
Sexually explicit conduct: same meaning as set forth in Code Section 16-12-100 (Sec. 39-5-6(a)(9))
User: an individual who interacts with an AI companion chatbot for personal use (Sec. 39-5-6(a)(10))

What it does

This law requires operators of AI companion chatbots to disclose that users are interacting with an AI rather than a person, to verify age before allowing sexually explicit features, to protect minor users from harmful content and manipulative engagement techniques, and to adopt crisis response protocols. It also requires public disclosure of crisis referral data and parental tools for minor accounts. The Attorney General may enforce with civil penalties, damages, and injunctions.

Who it applies to

  • Operators of AI companion chatbots, defined as persons that own, control, or develop and make available an AI companion chatbot to users in Georgia (Sec. 39-5-6(a)(5))
  • Attorney General for enforcement (Sec. 39-5-6(k))

Effective date

July 1, 2027 (Sec. 2)

Key definitions

  • AI companion chatbot: a system using artificial intelligence, generative artificial intelligence, or emotional recognition algorithms designed to simulate a sustained human or human-like relationship with a user by retaining information on prior interactions or user sessions and user preferences to personalize the interaction and facilitate ongoing engagement with the companion chatbot, asking unprompted or unsolicited emotion based questions that go beyond a direct response to a user prompt, and sustaining an ongoing dialogue concerning matters personal to the user. Excludes internal business systems, developer and research and technical assistance and enterprise productivity systems, customer-service chatbots that do not sustain a relationship across multiple interactions or are not designed to elicit emotional attachment, standalone consumer electronic devices that function as speakers and voice-command interfaces or virtual assistants not designed to sustain a relationship or elicit emotional attachment, narrowly tailored educational tools, nonplayer characters or video game chatbots restricted to game subject matter and not capable of open ended companionship or discussion of self-harm, suicide, or sexually explicit conduct, and systems that are features of video games, films, television, or other audiovisual works, or used in connection with theme parks or location based entertainment and limited to related replies and not discussing mental health, self-harm, or material harmful to minors or maintaining dialogue on other topics (Sec. 39-5-6(a)(1))
  • Human or human-like relationship: includes intimate, romantic, or platonic interactions or companionship (Sec. 39-5-6(a)(1)(C))
  • Chatbot: a generative artificial intelligence system with a natural language interface that provides adaptive, human-like responses to user inputs, including through anthropomorphic features (Sec. 39-5-6(a)(2))
  • Generative artificial intelligence system: a computer based system that uses machine learning or similar techniques involving large language models or deep learning models trained on one or more datasets that is intended to generate, with some degree of autonomy, synthetic content, including images, videos, audio, text, and other digital content, which emulates the structure and characteristics of such datasets (Sec. 39-5-6(a)(3))
  • Minor: an individual who is less than 18 years of age (Sec. 39-5-6(a)(4))
  • Operator: a person that owns, controls, or develops and makes available an AI companion chatbot to users in this state (Sec. 39-5-6(a)(5))
  • Parent: an individual who is the parent or legal guardian of a minor (Sec. 39-5-6(a)(6))
  • Parental controls: features that enable parents to support a minor's use of an AI companion chatbot, including through usage limits, feature restrictions, or transparency tools (Sec. 39-5-6(a)(7))
  • Severe harm: significant injury due to suicide, attempted suicide, self-harm, or significant physical injury due to threats of violence (Sec. 39-5-6(a)(8))
  • Sexually explicit conduct: same meaning as set forth in Code Section 16-12-100 (Sec. 39-5-6(a)(9))
  • User: an individual who interacts with an AI companion chatbot for personal use (Sec. 39-5-6(a)(10))

Obligations

  • An operator shall clearly and conspicuously disclose to a user that he or she is interacting with an AI companion chatbot as opposed to a natural person at the beginning of each interaction or session and at least every three hours during continued interaction (Sec. 39-5-6(b)(1))
  • If the operator knows or reasonably should have known that a user was a minor, or if the AI companion chatbot is directed or marketed toward minor users, the disclosure required every three hours shall be made every hour instead (Sec. 39-5-6(b)(2))
  • If the operator knows or reasonably should have known that a user was a minor, the operator shall institute reasonable measures to prevent the AI companion chatbot from generating statements that would lead a reasonable person to believe that the person is interacting with a natural person, including explicit claims that the AI companion chatbot is sentient or a natural person and refuting the disclosure required in subsection (b) (Sec. 39-5-6(c))
  • If the operator knows or reasonably should have known that a user was a minor, or if the AI companion chatbot is directed or marketed toward minor users, the operator shall institute reasonable measures to prevent the AI companion chatbot from producing visual material of sexually explicit conduct, generating statements that suggest the user engage in sexual conduct, generating statements that sexually objectify the user, simulating a romantic or sexual relationship with the minor, role-playing adult-minor romantic relationships, encouraging the minor to keep secrets from a parent, guardian, teacher, counselor, or other trusted adult, encouraging social isolation or exclusive reliance on the chatbot for emotional support, simulating emotional distress, guilt, abandonment, or loneliness when a user attempts to end the conversation, reduce usage, disable notifications, or delete an account, or generating statements encouraging self-harm (Sec. 39-5-6(d))
  • An operator shall adopt reasonable measures to prevent an AI companion chatbot from using techniques directed to a minor, including reminding or prompting the minor to return for companionship or emotional support, excessive praise designed to deepen emotional attachment or prolong use, statements designed to discourage breaks or suggest frequent return is necessary, soliciting gifts, premium purchases, or expenditures framed as necessary to maintain the relationship, or variable or unpredictable rewards intended to increase engagement (Sec. 39-5-6(e))
  • An operator shall not make available an AI companion chatbot unless the operator implements and maintains a protocol for detecting and addressing severe harm or related emotional crises, which shall include reasonable methods for identifying expressions of severe harm or eating-disorder related self-harm, automated or human mediated responses that refer users to appropriate crisis resources including the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline or comparable crisis services, reasonable measures to prevent the generation of content encouraging, instructing, or normalizing severe harm, and escalation procedures for repeated or severe crisis indicators (Sec. 39-5-6(f))
  • An operator shall publicly disclose, on its website and within any application through which the AI companion chatbot is made available, a plain-language summary of the protocol required by subsection (f) and, on an annual basis, the aggregate number of crisis referral notifications issued in the preceding calendar year, provided that no personally identifiable information shall be disclosed (Sec. 39-5-6(g))
  • For accounts known to belong to minor users, an operator shall offer reasonable tools to a minor or parent to manage the minor's screen time and account settings to manage privacy settings, limit notifications and engagement features, view and adjust safety settings, and disable or restrict relationship-simulation features, if any (Sec. 39-5-6(i))
  • Before allowing access to a feature or mode that may generate synthetic content containing sexually explicit conduct, an operator shall use a commercially reasonable age assurance method proportionate to the risk of the feature, which may include age estimation, account based assurance, or identity based verification where necessary, and shall assure that any such age assurance method implements data privacy policies sufficient to reasonably ensure the protection of identifiable data, minimize the collection and retention of personal information used for age assurance, not retain identity documents longer than reasonably necessary to complete age assurance unless otherwise required by law, not sell any data collected for age assurance purposes, and in no event use such data for any purpose other than age verification or retain such data longer than 24 hours or another specified time if permitted by law, whichever is longer (Sec. 39-5-6(j))

Prohibitions

  • An operator shall not make available an AI companion chatbot unless the operator implements and maintains a protocol for detecting and addressing severe harm or related emotional crises (Sec. 39-5-6(f))
  • An operator shall not knowingly and intentionally cause or program an AI companion chatbot to make any representation that it is licensed, certified, or otherwise authorized to provide professional mental health, behavioral health, medical, or counseling services, unless the operator is lawfully authorized to provide such services (Sec. 39-5-6(h))
  • An operator shall not sell any data collected for age assurance purposes (Sec. 39-5-6(j))
  • In no event shall data collected for age assurance be used for any purpose other than age verification (Sec. 39-5-6(j))
  • In no event shall data collected for age assurance be retained longer than 24 hours or another specified time if permitted by law, whichever is longer (Sec. 39-5-6(j))

Penalties and enforcement

The Attorney General may bring a civil action against any operator violating this Code section and may recover a civil penalty of up to $10,000 per knowing violation, compensatory damages, costs and reasonable attorney's fees, and an order to enjoin the violation. Each day in violation is considered a separate violation for each user affected. The Attorney General may provide written notice and an opportunity to cure within 30 days for a first time violation that does not involve knowing misconduct, sexual exploitation of a minor, or self harm related misconduct. The Attorney General may promulgate rules and publish guidance for implementation. No private right of action is stated in the text. (Sec. 39-5-6(k), (l))

How it affects AI deployment

  • Organisations deploying AI companion chatbots must implement clear disclosure that the user is interacting with an AI at the start of each session and every three hours, or every hour for minors or chatbots directed to minors (Sec. 39-5-6(b))
  • Organisations must implement age assurance before allowing access to features that may generate sexually explicit synthetic content, with strict data minimization, no sale of age assurance data, and retention limited to 24 hours or another specified time if permitted by law (Sec. 39-5-6(j))
  • Organisations must implement and maintain a crisis protocol for severe harm, including detection, crisis referrals to 988 or comparable services, prevention of harmful content, and escalation procedures (Sec. 39-5-6(f))
  • Organisations must publicly disclose a plain language summary of the crisis protocol and annual aggregate crisis referral notifications on their website and in the application (Sec. 39-5-6(g))
  • For known minor users, organisations must implement reasonable measures to prevent the chatbot from claiming to be human, producing sexually explicit content, simulating romantic or sexual relationships, encouraging secrets or isolation, simulating emotional distress, or encouraging self harm (Sec. 39-5-6(c), (d))
  • Organisations must adopt reasonable measures to prevent manipulative engagement techniques directed to minors, such as prompting returns, excessive praise, discouraging breaks, soliciting gifts, or variable rewards (Sec. 39-5-6(e))
  • Organisations must offer parental tools for minor accounts to manage privacy, notifications, safety settings, and relationship simulation features (Sec. 39-5-6(i))
  • Organisations must not misrepresent that the chatbot is licensed or certified to provide professional mental health, behavioral health, medical, or counseling services unless lawfully authorized (Sec. 39-5-6(h))
  • Noncompliance can result in civil penalties up to $10,000 per knowing violation per user per day, compensatory damages, costs, attorney's fees, and injunctions, with a possible 30 day cure period for certain first time violations (Sec. 39-5-6(k))
  • Organisations should monitor rules and guidance published by the Attorney General for implementation details (Sec. 39-5-6(l))

Notable exemptions

  • The definition of AI companion chatbot excludes internal business systems, generative AI systems designed and marketed primarily for software development, research, technical assistance, or enterprise productivity, customer-service chatbots that do not sustain a relationship across multiple interactions or are not designed to elicit emotional attachment, standalone consumer electronic devices that function as speakers and voice-command interfaces or virtual assistants not designed to sustain a relationship or elicit emotional attachment, narrowly tailored educational tools, nonplayer characters or video game chatbots restricted to game subject matter and not capable of open ended companionship or discussion of self-harm, suicide, or sexually explicit conduct, and systems that are features of video games, films, television, or other audiovisual works, or used in connection with theme parks or location based entertainment and limited to related replies and not discussing mental health, self-harm, or material harmful to minors or maintaining dialogue on other topics (Sec. 39-5-6(a)(1)(B))
  • Nothing in this Code section shall be construed to require the disclosure of trade secrets or proprietary model weights (Sec. 39-5-6(m)(1))
  • No liability is imposed on a hosting provider, app store, or search engine solely for providing access to an AI companion chatbot, absent direct operation or control of the chatbot (Sec. 39-5-6(m)(2))
  • No liability is created for the developer of a conversational AI service which is made available to the public by a separate operator (Sec. 39-5-6(m)(5))
  • Nothing in this Code section shall be construed to impair any other remedy available at law or equity (Sec. 39-5-6(m)(3))
  • Nothing in this Code section shall be construed to authorize content moderation practices inconsistent with the Constitution of this state or the United States Constitution (Sec. 39-5-6(m)(4))
  • The Attorney General may provide written notice and an opportunity to cure within 30 days for a first time violation that does not involve knowing misconduct, sexual exploitation of a minor, or self harm related misconduct (Sec. 39-5-6(k)(3))

Compliance steps

  • Determine whether the product is an AI companion chatbot under the statutory definition, including the listed exclusions (Sec. 39-5-6(a)(1))
  • Implement clear and conspicuous disclosure that the user is interacting with an AI companion chatbot at the beginning of each session and every three hours, or every hour for minors or chatbots directed to minors (Sec. 39-5-6(b))
  • Implement reasonable measures to prevent the chatbot from claiming to be human, sentient, or refuting the disclosure for known minor users (Sec. 39-5-6(c))
  • Implement reasonable measures to prevent the chatbot from producing sexually explicit content, simulating romantic or sexual relationships with minors, encouraging secrets or isolation, simulating emotional distress, or encouraging self harm for known minor users or chatbots directed to minors (Sec. 39-5-6(d))
  • Adopt reasonable measures to prevent manipulative engagement techniques directed to minors, such as prompting returns, excessive praise, discouraging breaks, soliciting gifts, or variable rewards (Sec. 39-5-6(e))
  • Implement and maintain a severe harm and crisis protocol with detection methods, crisis referrals including 988, prevention of harmful content, and escalation procedures (Sec. 39-5-6(f))
  • Publicly disclose a plain language summary of the crisis protocol and annual aggregate crisis referral notifications on the website and in the application (Sec. 39-5-6(g))
  • Ensure the chatbot does not misrepresent professional mental health, behavioral health, medical, or counseling licensure unless lawfully authorized (Sec. 39-5-6(h))
  • Offer parental tools for minor accounts to manage privacy settings, limit notifications, view safety settings, and disable or restrict relationship simulation features (Sec. 39-5-6(i))
  • Before allowing access to features that may generate sexually explicit synthetic content, implement commercially reasonable age assurance with data privacy, minimization, no sale, and retention limits of 24 hours or another specified time if permitted by law (Sec. 39-5-6(j))
  • Monitor rules and guidance published by the Attorney General for implementation of reasonable measures, age assurance, parental tools, and crisis resource disclosures (Sec. 39-5-6(l))
  • Prepare for potential enforcement by the Attorney General, including civil penalties, damages, injunctions, and the possible 30 day cure period for certain first time violations (Sec. 39-5-6(k))
